data.one_liner: Flutter bridge to initiate Sign in with Apple on iOS, macOS, Android, and Web.
data.what_it_does: Provides methods and widgets to sign users in using their Apple ID across iOS, macOS, Android, and Web. Also includes support for retrieving and managing keychain entries.
use_when: You need to implement Sign in with Apple authentication in your Flutter application.
Your app targets iOS, macOS, Android, and Web platforms.
avoid_when: You do not have a paid membership to the Apple Developer Program (required for Sign in with Apple).
You only need standard email/password or other social providers and do not require Apple authentication.
strengths: Supports multiple platforms including iOS, macOS, Android, and Web.
weaknesses: Requires a paid Apple Developer Program membership and extensive server-side integration for verification.
Android and Web setups require additional configuration (Service IDs, custom schemes, script tags).
data.setup_notes: Requires Apple Developer account setup (App ID, Service ID, cryptographic keys), configuring native capabilities in Xcode for iOS/macOS, adding a custom activity intent filter in AndroidManifest.xml for Android, and adding the Apple JS script tag for Web.

alternatives.name: firebase_auth
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose firebase_auth if you want a complete hosted backend solution that also supports Apple sign-in alongside other authentication providers.
